scripts.//test: Not a unit-test runner — this workspace has no units. It is two checks over claims the site makes that no other gate here can see, run in cost order. check-type-scale.ts is browser-driven and reads dist/, which is why apps/www/turbo.json adds this workspace's own `build` to the task's dependencies: a class name is a valid string whether or not it resolves to 9.9px, and only a browser knows which. check-cli-claims.ts reads source on both sides and needs no build at all — it binds the command reference to packages/cli/src/cli/commands/**, because the site stating a fact about the CLI that nothing checks is how three pages came to document commands that had been deleted while `share` shipped undocumented. Second because it is the cheap one and a failure here is a one-line fix, so a run that gets that far has already paid for the expensive half.
